notes: EBIT in this package is defined as GAAP operating income (reported as 'Operating income' in Expedia filings). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

D&A uses 'Total depreciation and amortization' from the cash-flow-related disclosure (Depreciation + amortization). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Capex uses 'Capital expenditures, including internal-use software and website development' from the consolidated statements of cash flows; values are converted to positive absolute dollars. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

NWC is computed as (Total current assets minus cash & restricted cash minus short-term investments) minus (Total current liabilities minus current maturities of long-term debt). Large negative NWC primarily reflects deferred merchant bookings (operating liability structure). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Cash in assumptions is 'cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash and cash equivalents' per the cash flow reconciliation to avoid undercounting cash-like balances; restricted cash was excluded from NWC by construction. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Tax rate is normalized to 0.20 because effective tax rates in filings include discrete/one-off effects (e.g., 2023 elevated effective tax rate); model uses a single base-case normalized rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))
Comps: forward P/E (NTM proxy) is taken from StockAnalysis; EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were not consistently available as NTM-labeled free data for these peers, so those fields are set to null.

NOL balance uses the disclosed state and foreign NOL carryforwards (approx.) summed; NOL utilization percent is held at 0.80 as a modeling default. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Sustained demand and lodging strength consistent with 2025 momentum (room nights and gross bookings growth) could keep revenue growth near the FY2026 guide range. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

Outperformance vs FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin expansion (+1.0 to +1.25 points) would support multiple and cash-flow expansion. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

Any improvement/deterioration in working-capital dynamics (deferred merchant bookings) could materially impact FCF conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Global travel marketplace connecting travelers, partners, and advertisers through Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo, with a large B2B travel business and advertising network. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

Revenue generated across merchant, agency, and advertising/media models; trivago contributes third-party advertising revenue. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

In FY2025, Expedia reported revenue of $14.733B and operating income (EBIT) of $1.871B, reflecting continued margin expansion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Liquidity profile includes $5.7B+ of cash & short-term investments at FY end, plus non-redeemable non-controlling interests (primarily tied to controlled subsidiaries). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 revenue was $14.733B (+8% y/y) with operating income (EBIT) of $1.871B (+42% y/y). ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

FY2026 outlook (from Q4 2025 release): revenue $15.6B–$16.0B (+6% to +9%) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of +1.0 to +1.25 points (full year). ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))
Market context: EXPE last price $235.18 (as of 2026-03-21).
investment_highlights: Base-case growth is anchored to management’s FY2026 revenue guidance and then tapers to more mature rates by 2030 (from 7.5% in 2026 down to 3.8% in 2030). ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

EBIT margin modeled near 12.6%–12.8%, consistent with the post-restructuring profitability level achieved in 2025 (EBIT margin ~12.7%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Investment intensity is held stable/declining (capex ~5.0%–5.2% of sales) while D&A remains ~5.9%–6.0% of sales, implying scalable technology spend. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))

Working capital is persistently negative due largely to deferred merchant bookings; base-case keeps NWC as a modestly improving negative percentage of sales (cash flow support, not zero). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442426000008/expe-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Operating risk from intense competition and pricing pressure across online travel agencies and metasearch platforms, which could limit margin expansion. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

Regulatory/legal and tax-related cost volatility (including reserves) could pressure EBIT margins relative to the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1324424/000132442425000008/expe-20241231.htm))

Macro/travel demand cyclicality and FX volatility can impact both growth and effective tax rate, affecting valuation outcomes. ([s202.q4cdn.com](https://s202.q4cdn.com/757635260/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Earnings-Release-Q4-2025_FINAL.pdf))

presentation.subtitle: Expedia Group (EXPE) — DCF inputs & comps (FY2023-2030)
valuation_summary: DCF base-case chains revenue growth to absolute forecast revenues (QA-ready via validation_support.forecast_revenue).
Terminal assumptions (2% terminal growth and 15.0x exit EBITDA multiple) are set to be economically sensible for a mature global travel marketplace rather than assuming outsized perpetual growth.
Comps are used primarily for forward earnings perspective (forward P/E); EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were not consistently available from the free peer sources used here (set to null).
